course_outline_concepts: Best-of-N SFT: distilling own best samples back into SFT
STaR (Zelikman 2022) as the original self-improvement SFT bridge
The iterative-SFT ↔ on-policy-RL crossover: when more SFT beats first RL round
Practical decision tree: when the right move is SFT, when RL, when alternation

sources.what_to_extract: The RSFT recipe as a recurring post-training pattern: sample N per prompt → score with RM or verifier → keep top → SFT → optionally repeat.
RLHF-V1..V5 schedule; V1..V3 = RSFT only; V4, V5 = PPO on top of RSFT checkpoints; K ~ 10+; dual RM (helpfulness + safety); PPO params lr=1e-6, KL=0.01, batch 512.
BoN-N at inference as a strong baseline vs PPO; BoN-KL formula log N − (N−1)/N; N ∈ {4, 16, 64}; reward-model overoptimization as the ceiling.
Zelikman 2022 rationale-bootstrap loop: generate rationale+answer → keep if answer correct → for wrong answers, rationalize backward given the correct answer → SFT on accepted → repeat.
ReST-EM as EM over latent rationale: E-step sample K=32, T=1.0, top-p=0.95, verifier-filter; M-step 1-epoch SFT lr=1e-5; saturation at 2 iters; diversity cap 4/problem.
Verifier-guided self-training: train a verifier on correct-vs-incorrect traces, let it filter future samples; failure traces become supervision.
Multi-round alternation is not incidental: Llama-2 5×(RSFT → PPO), Tülu-3 SFT→DPO→RLVR with reference resets; ablation cost 3–5 points on AlpacaEval/MT-Bench.
Actor-as-judge iterative DPO; 3-iter ceiling before reward drift; judge calibration improves with iteration.
Meta-judge breaks the 3-iter ceiling; length-bias control term; 4 iterations with continuing gains.
SPIN = iterative DPO with human text as chosen and previous-iter sample as rejected; SFT-only data can drive preference optimization.
Nash-MD framing: alignment as a two-player preference game; convergence under non-transitive preferences.
Six rounds of SFT → rejection sampling → DPO; K=10–30 rejection samples per prompt at T=0.6–1.0; DPO lr=1e-5, beta=0.1, NLL aux coeff=0.2; 50–80% synthetic rejection-sampled data per round.
Causal decomposition of pretrain/mid-train/RL; RL only helps at the edge of competence and when pretrain leaves headroom; mid-training ≈ extended SFT can beat RL-only at fixed compute.
